newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Hang Seng Index falls sharply in early trade.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng Index falls sharply in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fell a sharp 157 points, or 0.94 percent to 16,516, just after the start of trading on Friday morning, a much-needed correction after the market's record-breaking run, brokers said.
The index slid further to 16,482, a drop of 191 points.
Trading was active on turnover of HK$1.77 billion.
"This is just a correction after a strong run up," said Richard Verin, head of equities trading at Credit Suisse First Boston. "The (market's) tone is still good."
The index has set new records on seven of the past eight trading days.
"We are seeing buyers come in again on the lows," added Verin, citing the index's bounce off Thursday afternoon lows.
Hang Seng Index futures appeared to be trading in line with the cash market, and not leading it, brokers said.
The August contract was trading 125 points lower at 16,520 and the September contract 140 points lower at 16,580.
Brokers remained bullish on the outlook.
"After a consolidation, the market will move ahead again, said Adrian Ngan, director at Peregrine Securities. "The market has very good momentum."
Profit-taking in property shares was the major factor pulling the market down in early trade.
Cheung Kong shed HK$1.00 to trade at HK$95.75, but Hutchison Whampoa added HK$0.50 to HK$81.75. Henderson Land lost HK$1.25 to HK$75.25.
Blue chip conglomerate Swire Pacific dropped HK$0.50 to HK$71.50.
Red chips again suffered a bout of profit-taking, while H shares continued their strong rally.

The Hang Seng China Enterprises Index, the H share index of China-based state owned enterprises, gained 16.02 points, or 1.20 percent to 1,354.23, while the red chip Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index lost 27.73 points or 0.74 percent to 3,715.99.
Shanghai Industrial was trading HK$1.75 lower at HK$55.75 and COSCO Pacific lost HK$0.30 to HK$17.80.
